messages:
Alex K: Quick sync — v3.5.0 canary rolling. Change window closes 22:00 UTC. Deploybot has auto-rollback configured but want to confirm manual override rules and who signals a rollback. cc @Leah O @Maria S @Tariq A

deploy-bot: Canary started for v3.5.0 (slice=10%). Auto-rollback rules: p95 > 1.3x baseline for 5m OR error_rate > 0.5% for 3m. To change: set rollout.auto_rollback or use `/deploy override`. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback

Maria S: FYI production traffic is a bit noisy today, p95 blips expected around peak. Can we relax p95 threshold to 1.5x for this canary and keep error_rate strict?

Leah O: I'm +1 to keeping error_rate strict. Change-window note: if impact is customer-visible and window is ending, prefer manual rollback so we can coordinate comms.

Tariq A: We had a kvcache contention flake in staging last week. Can we add kvcache.read_errors > 0.05% as a rollback signal (or at least an alert)?

Jordan P: If we do manual rollback, pinned command is: `redwood deploy pin --env=prod --service=api-gateway --version=v3.4.9` — that will pin traffic and stop rollforward. Also runbook checklist: update release-notes, post to #incidents if customer-facing, create incident if >5% user failures.

Maria S: Applying temporary override to p95 threshold for this canary: `/deploy override set rollout.auto_rollback.p95=1.6x --reason="noisy traffic peak"` (will expire at 21:45 UTC).

deploy-bot: Override accepted. New auto-rollback p95 threshold = 1.6x until 21:45 UTC. Monitoring kvcache.read_errors as alert-only.

deploy-bot: Telemetry snapshot: canary p95 = 1.6x baseline (3m), error_rate = 0.12% (1m), kvcache.read_errors = 0.02% (5m). No auto-rollback triggered due to override.

Alex K: Seeing the p95 hit 1.6x — with override in place, do we still want to continue? Leah, what's your call given change window?

Leah O: Given override and low error_rate, hold for 10 more minutes, but prepare for manual rollback. Jordan, ready to pin if we see error_rate >0.5% or kvcache read errors spike.

sre-oncall: I'm watching traces. Most latency appears to be in the tokenization microservice (svc-tokenizer). I'll open a quick trace link in #eng-platform.

deploy-bot: Canary p95 now 1.7x (2m), error_rate 0.18% (2m). Note: override will expire at 21:45 UTC.

Tariq A: Tokenizer team pinged. They see increased GC due to a new dependency in v3.5.0. Mitigation: revert tokenizer flag `--token-buffer=8m` to `4m` helps. But that requires a deploy to that service, not the whole rollout.

Maria S: Given rolling canary hitting 1.7x and cross-service regression, I recommend manual rollback of v3.5.0 for the api-gateway slice to avoid wider exposure.

Alex K: Agreed. Jordan, execute manual pin and start customer comms. Call out: expected impact minimal, provide timeline to rollback completion.

Jordan P: Executing pin now: `redwood deploy pin --env=prod --service=api-gateway --version=v3.4.9 --reason="manual rollback - tokenizer latency"`

deploy-bot: Pin action successful. Traffic reverted for pinned service to v3.4.9. Canary halted.

Jordan P: Posting to #incidents and sending a brief to support: "Rolled back v3.5.0 on api-gateway due to tokenizer-related latency spike observed in canary. No customer-facing errors reported at scale. Monitoring continues."

Leah O: Good call. Follow-up items: 1) Product to update release-notes with the rollback note. 2) Tokenizer team to prepare a patch and perf test. 3) Devex to add kvcache.read_errors to rollback criteria. 4) Update runbook to require manual sign-off if change-window <30m left.

Maria S: I'll update the override expiry to cancel (it already expired when pin happened). Also logging the decision in the release ticket.

sre-oncall: I'll keep an eye for any aftershocks and confirm the rollforward plan once tokenizer patch is validated.

Alex K: Thanks everyone. Quick retrospective tomorrow — add to agenda: clarify thresholds vs noise, and add clearer owner for manual rollback during change windows. :thumbsup:"
